title: USDA Publishes Annual Dairy Import-Licensing Notices for the 2027 Quota Year
summary: USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service published two routine Federal Register notices on Sept. 2 governing the Dairy Tariff-Rate Quota (TRQ) import licensing program: one sets the 2027 license fee at $325 per license (total program cost estimated at $631,516 across roughly 1,950 licenses), and the other shifts specified quota amounts for certain dairy articles from the historical license category to the lottery (nonhistorical) category for the 2027 quota year.
why_it_matters: These are routine annual administrative filings, not a policy change, but they set the mechanics — fees and license-category allocations — for who can import quota-limited dairy ingredients in 2027. Worth a line in the trade-policy file given the active, high-profile US-Canada dairy tariff dispute already on the company's radar.
recommended_action: No action needed; file for reference alongside the broader US-Canada tariff tracking.

title: Survey Finds Rising Recall Volume Is Eroding Consumer Trust and Buying Behavior
summary: A consumer survey commissioned by GS1 US found FDA posted 26 food recall notices in August 2026 alone, and that 67% of consumers now say they've avoided an entire food category after just one recall notice, up from 60% a year earlier; 94% say they are concerned about how often food is recalled, and the share who believe the recall system effectively protects public health fell to 80% from 85%. GS1 US published the findings via a Sept. 2 press release, with same-day coverage from Fortune and Food Safety Magazine.
why_it_matters: Dairy products have accounted for a significant share of 2026's recall notices (cottage cheese, soft cheese tied to a multiyear Listeria outbreak, ice cream), so this data quantifies a real category-avoidance risk tied to recall volume and reinforces the case for clear, fast recall communications and proactive trust-building messaging.
recommended_action: Share the survey findings with communications and consumer-insights teams; use as supporting data when reviewing the recall-response and consumer-trust messaging playbook.
